extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, IP statisticians, researchers, and IP office staff using WIPO patent statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological notes for interpreting WIPO statistical indicators on patent applications, patents in force, utility models, PCT applications, and related patent-office procedural measures. Includes definitions, selection criteria, data limitations and calculation methods used in the World Intellectual Property Indicators 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data refer to published patent applications (18‑month publication lag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to published patent applications. There is a minimum 18-month delay between application date and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution when interpreting counts by application year because of the fixed lag between filing and publication; many figures and trends are based on published applications rather than filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IPC technology concordance table
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO’s International Patent Classification (IPC) technology concordance table was used to convert IPC symbols into 35 corresponding fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPC‑based mapping is the basis for assigning applications to technology fields; an electronic version of the concordance table is available at www.wipo.int/en/web/ip-statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of IPC-to-technology field correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence between International Patent Classification (IPC) symbols and technology fields is not always apparent (there is no one-to-one correspondence). It is therefore difficult to capture all the patents within a specific technology field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although IPC‑based definitions are likely to capture the vast majority of relevant patent applications, users should be aware of classification ambiguity and potential under/over‑coverage when analysing by technology field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and interpretation of Relative Specialization Index
rubrics_metrics.description: A positive relative specialization index value for a technology indicates that a country has a relatively high share of patent filings related to that technology field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative specialization index values are comparative indicators of a country's specialization in a technology; positive values indicate relative concentration, negative values indicate relative underrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of top origins/offices for displayed rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: The top 15 (or top 20) origins/offices were selected based on 2021–2023 total published applications (or other specified selection rules in each figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts and tables showing 'top N' origins/offices are produced according to the specified timeframe and selection criteria noted in the figure captions; check the caption to know the inclusion rule for that chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for energy‑related technology fields
rubrics_metrics.description: For definitions of the technologies – solar energy, fuel cell technology, wind energy technology, geothermal energy and hydro energy – see annex A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of classification ambiguity (no one-to-one mapping), the IPC‑based definitions in Annex A are used to approximate these technologies and are expected to capture the vast majority but not necessarily all relevant patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender attribution methodology for inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to attribute gender to inventors’ names recorded in PCT applications, WIPO produced a world gender–name dictionary based on information from 13 different public sources. Gender is attributed to a given name on a country‑by‑country basis, because certain names may be considered male in one country but female in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender attribution is name‑based and country‑contextualized; users should be aware of classification errors and cultural name ambiguities when interpreting gender statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caveat for 'share of applications granted'
rubrics_metrics.description: The share of applications granted should not be interpreted as a grant rate, as it is based on the examination date rather than the date when the application was filed. The number of grants in a given year relates to applications filed in previous years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because grants are counted by examination/grant year rather than filing year, comparisons or simple 'grant rate' inferences across years or offices may be misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross‑office comparability caution
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from IP offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. However, because of differences in procedure between patent offices, data cannot be fully harmonized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise caution when making comparisons across offices; procedural differences (e.g., whether examination is automatic or requested, reporting standards) affect indicators such as pending applications, grants, rejections and withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of pending applications to account for procedural differences
rubrics_metrics.description: To take account of procedural differences, pending application data are separated between (a) all patent applications, at any stage in the process, that are awaiting a final decision by a patent office, including those for which applicants have not filed a request for examination (where applicable), and (b) patent applications undergoing examination for which the applicant has requested examination (where such a request is necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should compare like‑with‑like (either 'all pending' or 'in examination') when analysing pending workloads across offices with differing procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of incomplete office data in graphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Data for some offices (e.g., China in certain graphs, EPO for rejected/withdrawn figures) are not included in specific charts when figures are unavailable or partial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing or partial data for large offices can materially affect world totals or rankings; check notes for omitted offices before interpreting a chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model data comparability caveat (China pre‑2017)
rubrics_metrics.description: China’s pre‑2017 data are not comparable owing to a change in methodology. Due to this break in the data series, and owing to the large number of filings in China, it is not possible to report accurately the 2017 growth rate at world level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious interpreting time series or growth rates that span methodology breaks for major contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin rule for utility model (UM) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a UM application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning origin to UM applications, use the first‑named applicant's residence; this rule is applied consistently in the presented UM tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of microorganism deposits for biotech patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits of microorganisms for patent procedures are important for biotechnological inventions. Disclosing an invention is a requirement for receiving a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an invention involves microorganisms that cannot be adequately described, deposits to an international depositary authority support the disclosure requirement of patent law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of patents in force calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The average age of patents in force is calculated using the following formula: Σ(p*y)/Σp, where p is the number of patents in force and y the number of years between filing and reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This weighted‑mean formula should be used to reproduce the reported 'average age' indicator for an office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patents in force as percentage of total applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as the number of patent applications filed in year t and in force in 2024, divided by the total number of patent applications filed in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all offices provide such historical in‑force data; figures are therefore based on available office data (e.g., data for 85 offices). Interpret sample coverage when generalizing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent prosecution highway (PPH) is a bilateral agreement between two offices enabling applicants to request a fast‑track examination whereby patent examiners can utilize work already undertaken by the other office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH request counts and flow charts show cross‑office use of accelerated examination; check figure captions for whether 'office of first filing' or 'office of earlier examination' labels are used (e.g., Japan figure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rules for top‑20 indicators based on GDP and population thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The top 20 origins were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 25 billion PPP and more than 100 resident patent applications (for patent per GDP indicator). For per‑capita indicators the top 20 were included if they had a population greater than 5 million and if they had more than 100 resident patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presented top‑20 lists are filtered by these economic/population and activity thresholds; results exclude jurisdictions not meeting thresholds or with missing macro data (e.g., ROK excluded for missing 2024 GDP).

rubrics_metrics.name: R&D and GDP data sourcing and lag
rubrics_metrics.description: GDP data are in 2021 US purchasing power parity (PPP) dollars. R&D data refer to gross domestic expenditure on research and experimental development (GERD) and R&D data lag by one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combining patent statistics with macroeconomic indicators, use the specified units and be mindful of the one‑year lag in R&D figures.
